source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Cincinnati CIN2 publishes 11 MW of IT capacity, enough for regional regulated workloads but not frontier AI training.

The facility pairs 11 MW with 143,778 square feet of technical space and holds PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and SSAE 16 Type II certifications. That certification set points to financial, healthcare, and federal tenants rather than machine learning workloads. The published capacity is the whole story here: 11 MW is a colocation-scale number, and the compliance profile fits the customers that scale serves.

Ohio has 77 mapped data center facilities, but only eight publish power figures. Those eight total 60.4 MW, and CIN2 alone accounts for 18 percent of that disclosed load. The concentration is an artifact of disclosure, not of Ohio's actual grid burden. Most of the state's facilities report nothing, so any share calculated against published totals describes the reporting population, not the state.

What this does not tell you is how much power Cincinnati actually draws, whether CyrusOne has expansion plans, or how CIN2 connects to the grid. The data covers one facility's published spec and its rank among a small, self-selected group of disclosers. Frontier training campuses now run past 100 MW, so 11 MW sits well below that threshold by the only measure given.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
